(Section)

Among the things that show the greatness of this surah, despite its brevity, is His swearing by al-'Asr (the afternoon, or time). Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "If all people were to reflect upon it, it would suffice them."

As for the al-'Asr by which He swears, it is said to be the beginning of the time of the day that follows the Maghrib (sunset); it is also said to be the last hour of the day; it is also said that what is meant is the 'Asr prayer. Most of the exegetes say that it is the dahr (time, the ages), and this is the preferred view. Calling dahr "'asr" is well known in their language. A poet said:

"The two 'asrs will not delay a day and a night
When they seek to overtake what they have aimed at."

Here "a day and a night" is an apposition (badal) for "the two 'asrs." So He swears by al-'Asr because of the lesson and sign in it. The passing of night and day, under the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing, is arranged for the interests of the world in the most perfect order and system; their alternation and balance at times, one taking from the other at times, their difference in light and darkness, heat and cold, the spreading and stillness of living creatures, and the division of time into centuries, years, months, days, hours and what is less than these, are all signs of the Lord, the Exalted, and proofs of His power and wisdom.

Thus He swears by al-'Asr, which is the time of human actions and their place, concerning the outcome of those actions and their recompense. By the beginning, which is the creation of time, the agents and their actions, He draws attention to the return (ma'ad), and that His power, which did not fall short in the beginning, does not fall short in the return. And His wisdom, which required the creation of time, the creation of agents and their actions, and making them of two kinds, good and evil, refuses to equate them, and refuses to recompense the doer of good with his good and the doer of evil with his evil, or to make both kinds profitable or losing. Rather, man, as man, is in loss, except for those whom Allah has mercied, guided and enabled to believe and do righteous deeds in themselves, and to command others to them. This is the counterpart of His returning man to the lowest of the low, and His exception of those who believe and do righteous deeds from those who are returned.

Reflect on the wisdom of the Qur'an: when it said ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾, it restricted and specified the exception, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience﴾. And when it said ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, it widened and generalized the exception, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, without saying "and advise one another," because mutual advice is the commanding of others to belief and righteous deeds, which is an additional degree beyond merely doing it. Whoever is not like that has lost this profit, and so is in loss, but it does not necessarily follow that he is in the lowest of the low. A person may fulfil what is obligatory upon him and not command others, for commanding right and forbidding wrong is an additional rank, which may be an individual obligation (fard 'ayn), a communal obligation (fard kifayah), or recommended (mustahabb).

"Advising one another to truth" includes the truth that is obligatory and the truth that is recommended; "advising one another to patience" includes the patience that is obligatory and the patience that is recommended. So those who advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience attain a profit which those lack who fulfilled what was obligatory upon them in themselves but did not command others to it, even though those were not among those who lost themselves and their families. The absolute "loss" is one thing, and "loss" in an absolute sense is another. He, the Exalted, said ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾, and one who profits in one commodity and loses in another may be called "in loss" and "one of loss," as 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "We have been negligent in many qirats." This is a kind of negligence, and a kind of loss relative to the one who gained that profit.

When He said in Surah al-Tin ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, He said ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, dividing people into these two categories only. Since man has two powers, the power of knowledge and the power of action, and two states, a state in which he is commanded by another and a state in which he commands another, Allah, the Exalted, excepted those whose knowledge-power is perfected by belief and whose action-power is perfected by righteous deeds, and who submit to the command of another and command others to it, from the man who is in loss. For the servant has two states: a state of perfection in himself, and a state of perfecting others. His perfection and his perfecting of others depend on two things:

knowledge of the truth, and patience upon it. So the verse includes all the ranks of human perfection: beneficial knowledge, righteous action, benefit to himself through these, benefit to his brother through them, and his submission and acceptance of one who commands him to them.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾ is a guidance to the station of leadership in the strength of religion, as in His saying ﴿And We made among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾. By patience and certainty leadership in religion is attained.

Patience is of two kinds: patience upon what is decreed, such as calamities, and patience upon what is legislated.

This second kind is also of two kinds: patience in obeying the commands, and patience in refraining from the prohibitions.

The first is patience toward will and act; the second is patience away from will and act.

As for the first kind of patience, it is shared between the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, and no reward is given for it by itself if it is not accompanied by faith and choice.

The Prophet ﷺ said concerning his daughter:

"Order her to be patient and to seek reward."

And Allah, the Exalted, said ﴿except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾.

And He said ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾.

And He said ﴿And if you are patient and fear Allah﴾.

So patience without faith and piety is like the strength of a body devoid of faith and piety. And in proportion to certainty about what is legislated, patience upon what is decreed follows.

And He, the Exalted, said ﴿So be patient, indeed the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾.

He commanded him to be patient and not to imitate those who have no certainty in lacking patience, for due to their lack of certainty they lacked patience, were flighty, and made their people flighty. Had they attained certainty and truth, they would have been patient, and would neither have been flighty nor made others flighty. Whoever's certainty is weak, his patience is weak; and whoever's patience is weak is light and easily moved. The certain, patient one is steady, for he has understanding and intellect; whoever has no certainty and no patience is light, frivolous, played with by desires and appetites as the winds play with a light object. And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

He heard a reciter reciting: ﴿By al-'Asr (1) Indeed, mankind is in loss (2) except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience (3)﴾

He said: "If all people took this surah, it would suffice them or be enough for them," just as al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If people reflected upon the surah of al-'Asr, it would suffice them."

For He, the Exalted, divided the human species into two kinds in it: losing and profiting. The profiting one is the one who advised his own self with belief and righteous action, and advised creation by counselling the truth, which includes teaching and guiding them, and counselling patience, which includes his own patience as well. So the surah includes the two advices and the two perfections, and the ultimate perfection of the two powers, in the most concise wording, most succinct, most refined, most beautiful in its style, and most subtle in its placement.

As for the two advices: the servant's advice to himself, and his advice to his brother by counselling the truth and patience upon it.

As for the two perfections: his perfecting himself and his perfecting his brother.

As for the perfection of the two powers: the soul has two powers, the power of knowledge and reflection, whose perfection is by faith, and the power of will, love and action, whose perfection is by righteous action, and this is not completed for it except by patience.

So here there are six matters: three he does in himself and commands others to do: perfecting his knowledge-power by faith, his action-power by righteous deeds, and persisting in that by patience upon it; and his commanding others to these three. Thus he is one who is obeyed in them, commanding them, characterized by them, teaching them, calling to them. This is the one who profits entirely, and whatever profit he has missed is in proportion to it, and he has gained some kind of loss. And Allah is the One sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

In "Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah" he said:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By al-'Asr, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If all people reflected upon this surah, it would suffice them."

The explanation of this: the ranks are four, and by completing them a person attains the utmost of his perfection:

The first: knowing the truth.

The second: acting upon it.

The third: teaching the one who does not know it well.

The fourth: patience upon learning it, acting upon it, and teaching it.

So the Exalted mentioned the four ranks in this surah, and He swore in this surah by al-'Asr that every person is in loss except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and these are those who knew the truth and affirmed it: this is one rank.

(and do righteous deeds): those who acted upon what they knew of the truth: this is another rank.

(and advise one another to truth): advising one another to it by teaching and guidance: this is a third rank.

(and advise one another to patience): they were patient upon the truth, and advised one another to be patient upon it and steadfast: this is a fourth rank.

This is the ultimate perfection, for perfection is that a person be perfect in himself and perfecting for others; his perfection is by reforming his two powers, the knowledge-power and the action-power: the soundness of the knowledge-power is by faith, the soundness of the action-power is by doing righteous deeds; and his perfecting of others is by teaching them and being patient with them, and advising them to patience in knowledge and action.

So this surah, despite its brevity, is among the most comprehensive of the Qur'an's surahs for all good in its entirety. Praise be to Allah, who made His Book sufficient against all else, a cure for every disease, a guide to every good.

In "Ighathat al-Lahfan" he said:

He, the Exalted, swore by time, which is the period of profitable and losing actions, that every one is in loss, except one whose knowledge-power is perfected by belief in Allah and whose action-power is perfected by acting in obedience to Him. This is his perfection in himself; then he perfects others by counselling them to that, commanding them to it, and to its foundation, which is patience. Thus he perfects himself by beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and perfects others by teaching them that and counselling them to be patient upon it.

In "al-Madarij" he said:

He, the Glorified, swore that every person is in loss, except one who perfects his knowledge-power by faith, and his action-power by righteous action, and perfects others by counselling the truth and patience upon it. The truth is faith and action, and they are not complete except by patience upon them. And by counselling one another to them, it is fitting for a person to spend the hours of his life, indeed his breaths, on what attains lofty goals and by which he is saved from manifest loss. This is achieved only by turning to the Qur'an, reflecting on it, pondering it, extracting its treasures, unearthing its hidden things, directing care toward it, and devoting one's resolve to it, for it is the guarantor of the servants' interests in this life and the next, and the one who conveys them to the path of right guidance. Thus the reality, the method, and the true spiritual states and experiences are all taken only from its niche, and are harvested only from its trees.

In "Uddat al-Sabirin" he said:

He, the Exalted, has judged loss as a general judgment upon everyone who does not believe and is not among the people of truth and patience.

This indicates that there is no profiter other than them. So He, the Exalted, said ﴿By al-'Asr, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾.

For this reason al-Shafi'i said: "If all people reflected upon this verse, it would suffice them."

This is because the servant's perfection lies in perfecting his two powers, the power of knowledge and the power of action, which are belief and righteous action.

Just as he needs to perfect himself, he needs to perfect others, which is mutual counselling to truth and mutual counselling to patience.

The foundation, base, and pillar upon which all this rests is patience.

(Benefit)

Know that religion is built upon two principles:

truth and patience, which are the two mentioned in His saying ﴿and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾.

Since what is required of the servant is to act upon the truth in himself and to implement it among people, and this is the reality of gratitude, he cannot do that except through patience upon it. So patience is half of faith. And Allah, the Exalted, knows best.

(Section)

Gathering with brothers is of two kinds:

One is gathering for the enjoyment of companionship and the filling of time; its harm outweighs its benefit, and at the least it corrupts the heart and wastes time.

The second is gathering with them for mutual help in the means of salvation, and counselling one another to truth and patience. This is among the greatest and most beneficial spoils, but it has three afflictions:

The first: some of them adorn themselves for others.

The second: speech and mixing beyond need.

The third: that this becomes a desire and habit by which one is cut off from the goal.

In sum, gathering and association are a cross-fertilization, either for the commanding soul (al-nafs al-ammarah) or for the heart and the soul at peace (al-nafs al-mutma'innah), and the result is derived from the cross-fertilization. Whoever seeks its cross-fertilization, his fruit is good.

Likewise, good spirits are cross-fertilized by the angel, and wicked ones by Satan, and Allah, the Glorified, by His wisdom, has made good things for good people and good people for good things.

This is the counterpart of His returning man to the lowest of the low, and His exception of those who believe and do righteous deeds from those who are returned.

Reflect on the wisdom of the Qur'an: when it said ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾, it restricted and specified the exception, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience﴾. And when it said ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, it widened and generalized the exception, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, without saying "and advise one another," because mutual advice is the commanding of others to belief and righteous deeds, which is an additional degree beyond merely doing it. Whoever is not like that has lost this profit, and so is in loss, but it does not necessarily follow that he is in the lowest of the low. A person may fulfil what is obligatory upon him and not command others, for commanding right and forbidding wrong is an additional rank, which may be an individual obligation (fard 'ayn), a communal obligation (fard kifayah), or recommended (mustahabb).

"Advising one another to truth" includes the truth that is obligatory and the truth that is recommended; "advising one another to patience" includes the patience that is obligatory and the patience that is recommended. So those who advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience attain a profit which those lack who fulfilled what was obligatory upon them in themselves but did not command others to it, even though those were not among those who lost themselves and their families. The absolute "loss" is one thing, and "loss" in an absolute sense is another. He, the Exalted, said ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾, and one who profits in one commodity and loses in another may be called "in loss" and "one of loss," as 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "We have been negligent in many qirats." This is a kind of negligence, and a kind of loss relative to the one who gained that profit.

When He said in Surah al-Tin ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, He said ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, dividing people into these two categories only. Since man has two powers, the power of knowledge and the power of action, and two states, a state in which he is commanded by another and a state in which he commands another, Allah, the Exalted, excepted those whose knowledge-power is perfected by belief and whose action-power is perfected by righteous deeds, and who submit to the command of another and command others to it, from the man who is in loss. For the servant has two states: a state of perfection in himself, and a state of perfecting others. His perfection and his perfecting of others depend on two things:

knowledge of the truth, and patience upon it. So the verse includes all the ranks of human perfection: beneficial knowledge, righteous action, benefit to himself through these, benefit to his brother through them, and his submission and acceptance of one who commands him to them.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾ is a guidance to the station of leadership in the strength of religion, as in His saying ﴿And We made among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾. By patience and certainty leadership in religion is attained.

Patience is of two kinds: patience upon what is decreed, such as calamities, and patience upon what is legislated.

This second kind is also of two kinds: patience in obeying the commands, and patience in refraining from the prohibitions.

The first is patience toward will and act; the second is patience away from will and act.

As for the first kind of patience, it is shared between the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, and no reward is given for it by itself if it is not accompanied by faith and choice.

The Prophet ﷺ said concerning his daughter:

"Order her to be patient and to seek reward."

And Allah, the Exalted, said ﴿except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾.

And He said ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾.

And He said ﴿And if you are patient and fear Allah﴾.

So patience without faith and piety is like the strength of a body devoid of faith and piety. And in proportion to certainty about what is legislated, patience upon what is decreed follows.

And He, the Exalted, said ﴿So be patient, indeed the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾.

He commanded him to be patient and not to imitate those who have no certainty in lacking patience, for due to their lack of certainty they lacked patience, were flighty, and made their people flighty. Had they attained certainty and truth, they would have been patient, and would neither have been flighty nor made others flighty. Whoever's certainty is weak, his patience is weak; and whoever's patience is weak is light and easily moved. The certain, patient one is steady, for he has understanding and intellect; whoever has no certainty and no patience is light, frivolous, played with by desires and appetites as the winds play with a light object. And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

He heard a reciter reciting: ﴿By al-'Asr (1) Indeed, mankind is in loss (2) except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience (3)﴾

He said: "If all people took this surah, it would suffice them or be enough for them," just as al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If people reflected upon the surah of al-'Asr, it would suffice them."

For He, the Exalted, divided the human species into two kinds in it: losing and profiting. The profiting one is the one who advised his own self with belief and righteous action, and advised creation by counselling the truth, which includes teaching and guiding them, and counselling patience, which includes his own patience as well. So the surah includes the two advices and the two perfections, and the ultimate perfection of the two powers, in the most concise wording, most succinct, most refined, most beautiful in its style, and most subtle in its placement.

As for the two advices: the servant's advice to himself, and his advice to his brother by counselling the truth and patience upon it.

As for the two perfections: his perfecting himself and his perfecting his brother.

As for the perfection of the two powers: the soul has two powers, the power of knowledge and reflection, whose perfection is by faith, and the power of will, love and action, whose perfection is by righteous action, and this is not completed for it except by patience.

So here there are six matters: three he does in himself and commands others to do: perfecting his knowledge-power by faith, his action-power by righteous deeds, and persisting in that by patience upon it; and his commanding others to these three. Thus he is one who is obeyed in them, commanding them, characterized by them, teaching them, calling to them. This is the one who profits entirely, and whatever profit he has missed is in proportion to it, and he has gained some kind of loss. And Allah is the One sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

In "Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah" he said:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By al-'Asr, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If all people reflected upon this surah, it would suffice them."

The explanation of this: the ranks are four, and by completing them a person attains the utmost of his perfection:

The first: knowing the truth.

The second: acting upon it.

The third: teaching the one who does not know it well.

The fourth: patience upon learning it, acting upon it, and teaching it.

So the Exalted mentioned the four ranks in this surah, and He swore in this surah by al-'Asr that every person is in loss except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and these are those who knew the truth and affirmed it: this is one rank.

(and do righteous deeds): those who acted upon what they knew of the truth: this is another rank.

(and advise one another to truth): advising one another to it by teaching and guidance: this is a third rank.

(and advise one another to patience): they were patient upon the truth, and advised one another to be patient upon it and steadfast: this is a fourth rank.

This is the ultimate perfection, for perfection is that a person be perfect in himself and perfecting for others; his perfection is by reforming his two powers, the knowledge-power and the action-power: the soundness of the knowledge-power is by faith, the soundness of the action-power is by doing righteous deeds; and his perfecting of others is by teaching them and being patient with them, and advising them to patience in knowledge and action.

So this surah, despite its brevity, is among the most comprehensive of the Qur'an's surahs for all good in its entirety. Praise be to Allah, who made His Book sufficient against all else, a cure for every disease, a guide to every good.

In "Ighathat al-Lahfan" he said:

He, the Exalted, swore by time, which is the period of profitable and losing actions, that every one is in loss, except one whose knowledge-power is perfected by belief in Allah and whose action-power is perfected by acting in obedience to Him. This is his perfection in himself; then he perfects others by counselling them to that, commanding them to it, and to its foundation, which is patience. Thus he perfects himself by beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and perfects others by teaching them that and counselling them to be patient upon it.

In "al-Madarij" he said:

He, the Glorified, swore that every person is in loss, except one who perfects his knowledge-power by faith, and his action-power by righteous action, and perfects others by counselling the truth and patience upon it. The truth is faith and action, and they are not complete except by patience upon them. And by counselling one another to them, it is fitting for a person to spend the hours of his life, indeed his breaths, on what attains lofty goals and by which he is saved from manifest loss. This is achieved only by turning to the Qur'an, reflecting on it, pondering it, extracting its treasures, unearthing its hidden things, directing care toward it, and devoting one's resolve to it, for it is the guarantor of the servants' interests in this life and the next, and the one who conveys them to the path of right guidance. Thus the reality, the method, and the true spiritual states and experiences are all taken only from its niche, and are harvested only from its trees.

In "Uddat al-Sabirin" he said:

He, the Exalted, has judged loss as a general judgment upon everyone who does not believe and is not among the people of truth and patience.

This indicates that there is no profiter other than them. So He, the Exalted, said ﴿By al-'Asr, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾.

For this reason al-Shafi'i said: "If all people reflected upon this verse, it would suffice them."

This is because the servant's perfection lies in perfecting his two powers, the power of knowledge and the power of action, which are belief and righteous action.

Just as he needs to perfect himself, he needs to perfect others, which is mutual counselling to truth and mutual counselling to patience.

The foundation, base, and pillar upon which all this rests is patience.

(Benefit)

Know that religion is built upon two principles:

truth and patience, which are the two mentioned in His saying ﴿and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾.

Since what is required of the servant is to act upon the truth in himself and to implement it among people, and this is the reality of gratitude, he cannot do that except through patience upon it. So patience is half of faith. And Allah, the Exalted, knows best.

(Section)

Gathering with brothers is of two kinds:

One is gathering for the enjoyment of companionship and the filling of time; its harm outweighs its benefit, and at the least it corrupts the heart and wastes time.

The second is gathering with them for mutual help in the means of salvation, and counselling one another to truth and patience. This is among the greatest and most beneficial spoils, but it has three afflictions:

The first: some of them adorn themselves for others.

The second: speech and mixing beyond need.

The third: that this becomes a desire and habit by which one is cut off from the goal.

In sum, gathering and association are a cross-fertilization, either for the commanding soul (al-nafs al-ammarah) or for the heart and the soul at peace (al-nafs al-mutma'innah), and the result is derived from the cross-fertilization. Whoever seeks its cross-fertilization, his fruit is good.

Likewise, good spirits are cross-fertilized by the angel, and wicked ones by Satan, and Allah, the Glorified, by His wisdom, has made good things for good people and good people for good things.
